questions.q: A Structured Streaming query reads from Kafka. Which option is required for every Kafka read, batch or streaming?

options.t: `kafka.group.id`, so Spark can commit offsets back to the Kafka cluster
options.why: Not required; the checkpoint tracks progress.

options.t: `kafka.bootstrap.servers`
`maxOffsetsPerTrigger`, so each micro-batch has a bounded size
options.why: A rate limit, not a required option.

options.t: `startingOffsets`, which has no default and must always be given explicitly
options.why: The required option is the bootstrap servers.

questions.explain: For both batch and streaming queries you must set kafka.bootstrap.servers, plus one of subscribe, subscribePattern or assign.

questions.q: A Kafka stream's `value` column must be parsed as JSON. What type does it arrive as?

options.t: VARIANT, already parsed from the JSON payload
options.why: The reader doesn't parse payloads.

options.t: A STRUCT inferred from the topic's Schema Registry subject
options.why: No schema is applied by the reader.

options.t: Binary: cast it to string and use from_json
STRING, already decoded with the topic's character set
options.why: Keys and values always arrive as byte arrays.

questions.explain: The reader returns key and value as binary (ByteArrayDeserializer); decode with cast('string'), from_json, from_avro or from_protobuf.

questions.q: A team needs to read every topic whose name starts with `orders-`. Which option fits?

options.t: `subscribe` with the value `orders-*` listed as a comma-separated topic
options.why: subscribe takes a list of topic names.

options.t: `assign` with a JSON object naming the prefix
options.why: assign takes specific topic partitions.

options.t: `topic` set to `orders-` on the reader
options.why: topic is a writer option.

options.t: `subscribePattern` with a Java regex

questions.explain: subscribe takes a topic list, subscribePattern a Java regex, assign specific partitions; exactly one of them is required.

questions.q: A Kafka topic must be loaded into a Delta table on a schedule, processing what arrived and then stopping. What does Databricks recommend?

options.t: A stream with `Trigger.AvailableNow`, tracked by its checkpoint
A continuous-processing trigger, stopped by the job's timeout
options.why: Continuous isn't supported on Databricks.

options.t: A stream with no trigger, killed by a cron job each hour
options.why: That isn't an orderly incremental batch.

options.t: A batch read with `startingOffsets` set by hand to the last offset read each run
options.why: That needs you to track offsets yourself.

questions.explain: The Kafka page: for incremental batch loading, Databricks recommends Kafka with Trigger.AvailableNow.

questions.q: A stream writes rows to Kafka with the writer option `topic` set to `alerts`, and the DataFrame also has a `topic` column. Where do the rows go?

options.t: To each row's own `topic` column value, ignoring the option
options.why: The writer option overrides a topic column.

options.t: To `alerts`: the option overrides any topic column
The write fails because both are set
options.why: It doesn't fail.

options.t: To both, duplicating every row
options.why: Rows are written once.

questions.explain: The writer's topic option sets the topic for all rows and overrides any topic column in the data.

questions.q: In Databricks SQL, how do you read a Kafka topic incrementally into a table?

options.t: `SELECT * FROM kafka.topic_name` against a foreign catalog
options.why: Kafka isn't a federation source.

options.t: `COPY INTO t FROM 'kafka://...'`
options.why: COPY INTO loads files.

options.t: A streaming table: `... AS SELECT ... FROM STREAM read_kafka(...)`
`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT * FROM read_kafka(...)` refreshed by a job
options.why: Streaming in SQL needs pipelines or streaming tables.

questions.explain: read_kafka is a table-valued function (DBR 13.3 LTS+). Streaming with SQL is supported only in Lakeflow pipelines or streaming tables.

questions.q: In the standard (gateway-based) SQL Server connector, what does the ingestion gateway do?

options.t: Runs once a day to copy a full snapshot of every table into the staging volume
options.why: The gateway runs continuously.

options.t: Translates T-SQL into Spark SQL for the pipeline

options.t: Hosts a read replica of SQL Server in Databricks
options.why: It isn't a database.

options.t: Runs continuously and manages the staging volume the pipeline reads from

questions.explain: Standard CDC has two parts: an ingestion gateway that runs continuously and manages a staging volume, and an ingestion pipeline that references it. Integrated CDC uses one pipeline.

questions.q: With integrated CDC for SQL Server, what does the single pipeline reference?

options.t: A Unity Catalog connection
A JDBC URL typed into the notebook
options.why: Credentials live in a UC connection.

options.t: An external location for the database files
options.why: The source is a database, reached through a connection.

options.t: An ingestion gateway's ID
options.why: That is the standard, gateway-based architecture.

questions.explain: Integrated CDC creates one pipeline that references a Unity Catalog connection and embeds extraction in each update.

questions.q: A column is renamed in a SQL Server table ingested with Lakeflow Connect. What does the connector's page say?

options.t: Renames are applied automatically, like new columns
options.why: New and deleted columns are supported; renames aren't.

options.t: Renames require a full refresh
The pipeline ignores the column from then on
options.why: It isn't ignored; a full refresh is needed.

options.t: The gateway rewrites the column name in staging
options.why: Nothing rewrites it.

questions.explain: New and deleted columns are supported; column renames aren't and require a full refresh.

questions.q: What kind of access does Lakehouse Federation give to an external PostgreSQL database?

options.t: Read and write, with Unity Catalog grants on each table
options.why: Federation is read-only.

options.t: A nightly copy into managed Delta tables
options.why: It queries in place.

options.t: Governed, read-only access through a foreign catalog
Ungoverned access through the database's own users only
options.why: Access is governed by Unity Catalog.

questions.explain: Lakehouse Federation gives governed, read-only access to external data through Unity Catalog foreign catalogs, with query pushdown.

questions.q: What is the difference between query federation and catalog federation?

options.t: Query federation is read-only, while catalog federation can also write changes back to the source catalog's tables
options.why: Both are read-only.

options.t: Catalog federation works only for databases; query federation only for files
options.why: It is the other way round in spirit: catalog federation reads table files.

options.t: They are two names for the same feature
options.why: They are different paths.

options.t: Query federation pushes queries to the database over JDBC; catalog federation reads the tables in object storage on Databricks compute

questions.explain: Query federation runs on Databricks and the remote database via JDBC; catalog federation (Hive metastore, Glue, Snowflake ...) reads directly from object storage and is more cost-effective.

questions.q: A source supports both Lakehouse Federation and Lakeflow Connect, and the team needs high volumes at low latency. What does Databricks recommend?

options.t: Lakeflow Connect
Either; they perform the same
options.why: The page recommends Lakeflow Connect for this case.

options.t: Lakehouse Federation, because it copies no data
options.why: For high volume and low latency the advice is Lakeflow Connect.

options.t: A Spark JDBC read in a notebook for every query
options.why: Not the recommendation.

questions.explain: When a source supports both, Databricks recommends Lakeflow Connect if performance on higher data volumes and lower latency are priorities.

questions.q: In what order is query federation set up?

options.t: Foreign catalog first, then the connection that serves it, then grants on the catalog
options.why: The connection comes first.

options.t: Connection (credentials and JDBC URL), then foreign catalog, then grants
External location, then volume, then COPY INTO
options.why: That is file ingestion.

options.t: Grants, then connection, then catalog
options.why: You can't grant on a catalog that doesn't exist.

questions.explain: Create a connection with credentials and the JDBC URL, create a foreign catalog using it, grant privileges, then query; queries are pushed down.

questions.q: A table in an AWS Glue catalog is read in Databricks as a foreign Iceberg table. Can a Databricks job write to it?

options.why: The REST API is for UC tables; foreign Iceberg tables are read-only in Databricks.

options.t: No: foreign Iceberg tables are read-only in Databricks
Only with deletion vectors enabled
options.why: Unrelated.

questions.explain: Foreign Iceberg tables are managed by a catalog outside Unity Catalog and are read-only in Databricks; managed Iceberg tables are created in Unity Catalog.

questions.q: How do external engines such as Spark, Flink or Trino read and write managed Iceberg tables in Unity Catalog?

options.t: By reading the table's Parquet files directly with storage keys
options.why: UC privileges aren't enforced on direct file access; the REST catalog is the documented path.

options.t: They can't; managed Iceberg tables are Databricks-only
options.why: The REST Catalog API serves external engines.

options.t: Through the Iceberg REST Catalog API, with credential vending

questions.explain: All Iceberg tables in Unity Catalog are reachable through the Iceberg REST Catalog API, which supports reads and writes and vends temporary credentials.

questions.q: Which file detection mode does Databricks recommend for most Auto Loader workloads?

Directory listing, because it needs only read access

questions.q: An Auto Loader stream must keep running when new columns appear, without adding them, and keep their values. Which mode?

none, which also rescues the values by default

questions.explain: rescue never evolves the schema or fails the stream; values for new columns go to the rescued data column.
